newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Evans D rated a buy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Evans D rated a buy.

text.p: Morgan Stockbroking Ltd said it placed a buy recommendation on engineering group Evans Deakin Industries Ltd based on an upgrade of profit forecasts for the current year and an expectation of strong medium-term profit growth.
"Recommendation is buy. We have upgraded our forecasts for 1996/97 and strong profit growth is expected to emerge over the medium term," Morgan analyst John Clifford said in a report.
"The outlook for earnings is positive with key markets such as mining, construction, power generation and transport forecast to remain buoyant," he said.
Clifford upgraded his profit forecast for the year ending June 30, 1997, to A$23.3 million from an earlier expectation of A$20 million and a reported A$14.1 million in 1995/96.
Clifford said the integration of Clyde Industries Ltd into the EDI group was proceeding well, following the acquisition earlier this year.
"The combined group will be a major force in engineering in Australia with annual sales in excess of A$750 million," Clifford said.
Clifford said Evans Deakin's consolidated balance sheet was carrying net debt of about A$98 million, giving a gearing ratio of 52 percent.
With funds from the sale of Clyde Chemicals to be applied towards debt reduction, gearing was expected to fall to about 25 percent, Clifford said.
Interest cover was forecast to remain at a comfortable 5.4 times in the current year.
He said the Clyde acquisition made strategic sense given that both companies had strengths in rail and resource-related products while direct competition was minimal.
Clyde also increased EDI's diversification through the non-engineering divisions of B&D Rollerdoors and industrial products.
Clifford said the real benefits from Clyde's acquisition would start to emerge in 1997/98 following re-focusing of the railway business.
"We believe there is substantial upside in earnings from these levels," Clifford said.
Evans Deakin shares last traded at A$3.40 by 0310 GMT on Tuesday, down one cent on Monday's close.
